They were created by a specific constitutional amendment listing each committee
They exist only due to a Supreme Court direction
advanced.e: Parliamentary Committees are not separately named in the constitutional text; they derive their existence from the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of each House, framed under Article 118, which empowers each House to regulate its own procedure, including constitution of committees.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements best reflects a nuanced understanding of the effectiveness of DRSCs in enhancing legislative scrutiny, as often discussed in the context of declining time spent by Parliament on detailed floor debate of bills?
o: DRSCs have completely replaced the need for floor debate on any Bill

DRSCs strengthen scrutiny by allowing detailed, non-partisan, in-camera examination of Bills and Demands for Grants away from the adversarial floor of the House, though referral of Bills to them is not mandatory in every case, which can dilute their intended role if bills are passed without such scrutiny
DRSCs are advisory bodies whose reports are legally binding on the government
DRSCs can amend a Bill directly without reference back to the House
advanced.e: DRSCs enable more detailed, less adversarial, in-camera scrutiny of Bills and Demands for Grants; however, since referring a Bill to a DRSC is not mandatory, several bills have been passed in recent years without such scrutiny, a point of criticism regarding the erosion of legislative scrutiny quality.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains the distinction between the roles of the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) and the Rules Committee in the Lok Sabha?
o: The BAC allocates time for business already on the agenda, while the Rules Committee frames/amends the procedural rules that govern how business is conducted, making them complementary but functionally distinct
Both committees perform an identical function of scrutinising public expenditure
The Rules Committee decides which Bills are Money Bills
The BAC frames the Rules of Procedure while the Rules Committee only allocates time
advanced.e: The Business Advisory Committee is concerned with the practical scheduling/time allocation of business, whereas the Rules Committee deals with the substantive procedural rules under which the House conducts all its business — a scheduling function versus a rule-making function.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the CAG's audit reports and the PAC's examination are together regarded as a crucial check on the executive's financial accountability under India's parliamentary system?
o: Because the CAG can strike down illegal government expenditure on its own authority

Because the CAG (an independent constitutional authority under Article 148) provides an external, professional audit, and the PAC (a body of the legislature) translates those findings into political accountability through Parliament, together forming a two-stage check on the executive's use of public funds sanctioned via the Appropriation Act
Because the PAC's decisions are appealable to the Supreme Court under Article 32
Because the CAG appoints members of the PAC directly
advanced.e: The CAG, an independent constitutional authority under Article 148, audits government expenditure and reports to Parliament; the PAC then examines these reports to enforce political and legislative accountability, together forming a robust two-stage mechanism ensuring public money is spent as authorised by the Appropriation Act.

advanced.q: Which of the following best captures a key criticism regarding the composition and continuity of Standing Committees like the PAC, Estimates Committee, and DRSCs, given their one-year tenure?
o: The annual reconstitution can disrupt continuity of expertise and follow-up on ongoing examinations, though it also allows wider rotation of members and prevents excessive concentration of committee power in a small group over a full term
Annual reconstitution has no effect on committee functioning since members never change
These committees have a fixed five-year, non-renewable tenure identical to the Lok Sabha's term
Annual tenure was introduced only after the 2019 general election
advanced.e: The one-year tenure and annual reconstitution of committees like PAC, Estimates Committee, and DRSCs is often flagged as a concern for continuity of subject expertise and follow-through on long, complex examinations, though it does allow broader member rotation and guards against long-term entrenchment of committee leadership.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why a report of a Parliamentary Committee, though not law, can nonetheless carry significant weight in subsequent judicial or executive action?
o: Because committee reports are automatically deemed statutes under Article 245

Because committee reports, being the product of detailed, cross-party legislative scrutiny, often shape public discourse, trigger executive follow-up (Action Taken Reports), and may sometimes be referred to by courts as persuasive material reflecting legislative intent or factual findings, even though they lack the force of law
Because the President is bound to implement every committee recommendation under Article 74
Because failure to implement a committee report is a ground for a no-confidence motion under Article 75(3) automatically
advanced.e: While not legally binding, committee reports — being outcomes of detailed, often cross-party scrutiny — carry persuasive and political weight; they can shape policy debate, compel an Action Taken Report from the government, and are occasionally cited as background/persuasive material, without themselves acquiring the force of law.
